company_name: Carnival Corporation Ltd. (formerly Carnival Corporation & plc)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,344.6M common shares outstanding at 2026-09-22 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover) + ~5M dilutive RSUs (Q3 diluted 1,368M vs basic 1,363M weighted). The 2027 convertible notes were settled in Dec 2025 (69.1M shares issued + $500M cash) and no convertibles remain in the debt table, so no further conversion dilution. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the $2.5B buyback ($929M spent 9M FY2026) is the cash mechanism, not an extra credit.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement share-based compensation $98M; 10-Q Q3 FY2026 nine-month $73M vs $70M prior; TTM to Aug-2026 = 98 - 70 + 73 = $101M. Equity-award tax withholding not separately material (vested awards settled from treasury shares, non-cash).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%. Unlevered leisure/travel asset beta ~1.05 relevered at market D/E ~0.57 with no tax shield (Section 883 / tonnage tax: cash tax ~0.5% of pre-tax) -> equity beta ~1.65, CoE ~12.5%. Pre-tax = post-tax cost of debt ~5.5%, reflecting the 2026 investment-grade ratings (Fitch, then S&P in Q3 FY2026) and the 5.1-6.1% coupons on the refinanced unsecured notes; pre-upgrade high-yield debt at ~7% would have put WACC near 10.5%. Weights at market: equity ~$39.9B (64%), net debt ~$22.7B (36%) -> WACC ~10.0%. The same 10.0% is used in all three scenarios: unhedged fuel, Caribbean overcapacity and macro/pandemic shock risk are carried in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, NOT as a WACC premium (risk charged once, adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), by construction under US GAAP: operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA, so operating lease liabilities ($168M current + $1,082M non-current = $1,250M at 2026-08-31) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Ships are owned, not leased; no finance-lease adjustment needed. lease_cost_pct_path left at zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (SKILL.md routing: operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Carnival is an asset-heavy operating company whose value is a stream of unlevered free cash flow; none of the non-FCF rows (bank, REIT, LIC, holdco, distressed, live deal) apply - the May 2026 DLC unification is complete and is not a pending corporate action. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). FY0 = FY2026E (year ends 30-Nov-2026, three weeks after the valuation date): revenue $27,850M = 9M actual $21,263M + Q4 at FY2025 Q4 ($6,330M) +4%; FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guided ~$7.14B (25.6% post-SBC, 26.0% pre-SBC), depressed ~1.5pp by the Iran-conflict fuel spike (fuel ~$2.15B, unhedged). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027, because the Aug-2026 net debt already contains nine months of FY2026 cash flow - starting the flows at FY2026 would count those months twice. EBITDA in this model is PRE-SBC (reported EBITDA = operating income + D&A already carries SBC expense, so the margin path adds back ~0.37pp and the engine deducts it once). last_fcf/reported_fcf are TTM to Q3 FY2026 (OCF 6,821 - capex 3,645) and are LEVERED (after ~$1.15B cash interest); the engine flows are unlevered, which is why net debt is deducted in full. Net debt uses balance-sheet carrying debt $23,912M; face principal is $24,559M (unamortised issuance costs/discounts $647M) - using face would lower value ~$0.48/share. Interest income ($41M 9M FY2026) not stripped: the company holds net debt, not net cash. Buyback note: CCL is a repurchaser ($929M 9M FY2026, avg ~$27/share in Q3), so the flat count is being funded. Cash tax: Section 883 and UK/Italian tonnage tax keep cash tax under 1% of pre-tax income (FY2025 $12M on $2,772M); paths drift up to allow for Pillar Two / Bermuda CIT exposure on non-shipping income. Capex: FY2026E ~$2.95B (10.6% of revenue) is a light year; contracted newbuild commitments are $1.6B FY2027, $1.5B FY2028, $1.8B FY2029 on top of ~$2.2-2.4B/yr of ship enhancements and Paradise Collection destinations, so base capex is 13.5-14% of revenue - above D&A (10.5%) because replacement cost of a 94-ship fleet exceeds its historical-cost depreciation. Working capital: customer deposits (~$7.1-8.5B, ~26% of revenue) grow with bookings, modelled as 25% capture on the revenue CHANGE (positive sign: prepaid model, structural $9.1B WC deficit).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue FY2019-FY2025 6-year CAGR (pre-pandemic peak to latest full year), because every 3- and 5-year window starts inside the 2020-2022 shutdown
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (20.2%) and 5yr CAGR (-9.8%) diverge >30% from revenue CAGRs (29.8% / 36.6%); both series are dominated by the COVID shutdown and recovery (equity fell from $25.4B FY2019 to $7.1B FY2022 via ~$29B of losses and is being rebuilt from earnings). Book-value CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined over 3 and 5 years (negative starting values: FY2022 EPS -5.16, owner FCF -6,711; FY2020 owner FCF -10,026). Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC): FY2023 $944M, FY2024 $1,235M, FY2025 $2,509M, TTM Q3 FY2026 $3,075M - the 2-year FY2023-FY2025 CAGR of 63% is recovery, not a run-rate. SBC is small (~0.4% of revenue) and growing roughly with revenue, so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF trajectories do not diverge. Pre-pandemic revenue CAGR FY2014-FY2019 was 5.6% with ~4-5%/yr capacity growth; the current newbuild book (7 ships through 2033) implies ~1%/yr net capacity growth, so forward growth is mostly yield.

base.narrative: Yield-led growth on ~1% capacity: FY2027 +4.5% (record 2027 book at higher pricing, offset by Caribbean capacity additions), easing to 3% by FY2033. Fuel normalises only partly from the FY2026 spike, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from 26.0% to 27.7% (FY2025 level) by FY2028-29 and settles at 28.3%, below the 2016-2018 peak of 28-29%. Capex 13.5-14% of revenue funds the contracted newbuilds and destinations. Cap 12x (cyclical) binds over a 13.7x Gordon.

bull.narrative: Price-to-value gap closes faster: Celebration Key / Paradise Collection lift onboard spend, AI yield management and record 2027-28 bookings drive 5-6% revenue growth on minimal capacity; fuel retreats to pre-spike levels and the cost discipline that beat FY2026 guidance by >$150M persists, taking pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 30% (above the 2016 peak, consistent with the 19-year-high ROIC). S&P 500 inclusion and IG ratings are financing tailwinds, already in the 10% WACC.

bear.narrative: Unhedged fuel stays elevated (Middle East disruption; a 10% fuel move is ~$145M of net income for CCL vs ~$57M for RCL) while double-digit Caribbean capacity growth and a consumer recession in FY2028 cut yields: revenue +1% then -4%, pre-SBC EBITDA margin troughs at 21.5% and only recovers to 25% (FY2019 level less EU ETS/FuelEU/IMO costs at full phase-in). Contracted euro newbuild payments keep capex at 15% through the trough. No solvency event: ~$5.7B liquidity and IG ratings make this an earnings and multiple bear, not a 2020 replay.

scenario_narratives.base: Carnival grows on yield, not ships: ~1%/yr capacity from a 7-ship newbuild book plus 3-4% pricing and onboard gains, with Celebration Key and the Paradise Collection adding high-margin destination revenue. Fuel stays above FY2025 levels but below the March-2026 spike, and pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs back to ~28% - recovered, not record. Free cash flow of ~$4B/yr in FY2027 rising to ~$5.7B by FY2036 is split between deleveraging, the $2.5B buyback and the dividend; none of that capital-allocation choice is credited separately because buybacks are value-neutral at intrinsic value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Close-in demand and record 2027-28 bookings validate the price-to-value-gap thesis; exclusive destinations and AI-driven yield management lift revenue 5-6%/yr for three years, fuel normalises, cost discipline holds, and margin reaches 30% - above the 2016-2018 peak. Investment-grade status cuts refinancing costs and the simplified single listing brings index inflows (a price, not a value, effect).
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes that hurt Carnival specifically: unhedged fuel (2.5x RCL's earnings sensitivity) stays high, industry Caribbean capacity floods pricing, and a 2028 recession hits a high-fixed-cost fleet with ~$22.7B of net debt. Margins trough at 21.5% and stabilise at 25% as decarbonisation costs (EU ETS at 100%, FuelEU, possible IMO Net Zero Framework) become structural. Liquidity of $5.7B and IG ratings keep it a going concern; the cost is equity value, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: CCL is the only big-four cruise operator with no fuel hedge, it carries ~3x net debt/EBITDA on a high-operating-leverage fleet, and the cruise industry has had two existential-scale shocks (2008-09, 2020-21) in seventeen years. Base 50% reflects the raised FY2026 guidance and record forward bookings. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs fuel normalisation, sustained pricing against heavy Caribbean supply AND margins above the pre-pandemic peak at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF at a 10.0% USD WACC on a component build, FY2027-FY2036 horizon, terminal value capped at 11-13x FCF for a cyclical, deducting $22.7B of balance-sheet net debt at 31-Aug-2026. SBC is expensed and the share count held flat. Risk is carried in the flows and the 25% bear weight - fuel, overcapacity and recession are scenario drivers - not in a WACC premium; the 2026 investment-grade upgrades enter only through the ~5.5% cost of debt. Because equity is ~64% of EV, every 1% of enterprise value moves the per-share value ~1.6%: the leverage that made the recovery trade is still the dominant sensitivity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fuel: unhedged; ~$145M of net income per 10% move in fuel cost per tonne (FY2026 fuel ~$2.15B). Each 1pp of EBITDA margin is ~$290M/yr of FCF and roughly $1.80/share.
Leverage amplifies EV errors: net debt is ~36% of EV, so a 10% EV miss is a ~16% equity miss.
Capex intensity: the model holds 13.5-15% of revenue; if fleet replacement at today's shipyard prices requires the pre-pandemic 16-19%, value falls materially.
Tax regime: Section 883 / tonnage-tax status underpins a near-zero cash tax rate; loss of the publicly-traded test or a broadening of Pillar Two to shipping income is not in the base case.
Terminal cap binds in base (12x over a 13.7x Gordon): terminal value is ~half of EV, so the cap choice is itself a key input.
Event risk (pandemic, war, incident) is only partly captured by a single recession-shaped bear case.
